disease_label_per_paper: Disseminated Histoplasmosis Found in Bone Marrow in a Newly Diagnosed AIDS Patient

demographics.country_or_region_context: recent immigration from Central Mexico to Southern California

presentation_summary: 31-year-old man with a history of anemia presented to the emergency department with progressively worsening abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea for four to five days.
He had recently immigrated from Central Mexico, had oral thrush on examination, and was newly diagnosed with AIDS with CD4 count 41 cells/uL and HIV RNA 369,000 copies/mL.
Initial presentation was sepsis-like with respiratory rate 24/min, blood pressure 96/54 mmHg, qSOFA 2, pancytopenia, and lactate 2.35 mmol/L.
Urine Histoplasma antigen later returned positive, and bone marrow biopsy plus culture confirmed Histoplasma capsulatum.

The patient initially received antibacterial therapy and fluconazole, started ART, later declined IV amphotericin after diagnosis, was switched to itraconazole, and was readmitted around three months later for sepsis/headache and given liposomal amphotericin B.

actual_treatment: ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily, metronidazole 500 mg every 8 hours, and fluconazole 800 mg orally daily empirically
bictegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir started after HIV diagnosis
TMP-SMX added then stopped after diffuse pruritic maculopapular rash
clindamycin and primaquine for PJP prophylaxis
after bone marrow confirmation, IV amphotericin was offered for severe histoplasmosis but the patient refused
fluconazole changed to itraconazole loading dose 200 mg three times daily for three days, then 200 mg daily
around three months later, readmitted for sepsis and headache and received an eight-day course of liposomal amphotericin B at 5 mg/kg

outcome.source_text_value: Approximately three months after discharge, the patient was readmitted for sepsis, with a new complaint of headache ... the patient continues to remain compliant with ... itraconazole

quality_warnings: Histoplasma urine antigen, bone marrow biopsy, and bone marrow culture are stored only in confirmatory_findings, not ordinary observations.
The paper does not report initial temperature, heart rate, oxygen saturation, CRP, AST/ALT, bilirubin, ferritin, or imaging findings at the initial presentation.
HIV RNA and CD4 are structured because they are host-risk context, not Histoplasma-confirmatory evidence.
The patient's later readmission and amphotericin course are preserved as course/treatment context rather than initial presentation evidence.
CD4 count, HIV RNA, and AIDS activity are preserved as host-risk context rather than ordinary histoplasmosis likelihood observations.
